title: Content, organic & email

entries.title: Instagram Reels: score every reel on watch time, sends per reach and likes per reach
entries.guidance: Instagram leadership said in January 2025 that its top three ranking signals are watch time, likes and sends. Sends count slightly more for reaching non-followers, and likes count slightly more for reaching existing followers. Instagram's ranking explainer says Reels are ranked on how likely a viewer is to reshare, watch to the end, like, or open the audio page. It also says viewers are surveyed on whether a reel was worth their time. The useful per-reel KPIs are therefore average watch time, sends divided by reach, and likes divided by reach, not raw views or comment counts (comments were not named as a top signal). Instagram shows fewer reels that are low-resolution, watermarked, muted, bordered, mostly text, or already posted on Instagram. Its 2025 creator tips say to post consistently and make every reel understandable to a stranger who has never seen the account.
do: Build a per-reel scorecard: reach, average watch time, sends/reach, likes/reach, follows
Write 'forwardable' content for growth (a checklist, a framework or a sharp take a viewer would send to a specific friend or peer)
Make each reel standalone: no 'as I said in part 1' openings
Use audio (voice or music) and upload natively at full resolution
dont: Repost clips with another app's watermark or add borders/letterboxing
Publish muted or text-wall reels
Optimise for comment volume alone as the primary KPI
Judge a reel by views without normalising by reach
steps: 48-72h after posting, pull reach, average watch time, sends, likes and follows from Insights
Compute sends/reach and likes/reach
Compare each reel with the account's trailing 10-reel median and flag the top and bottom 20%
Re-cut top performers into new hook variants (see trial reels entry), and diagnose bottom performers on the first 3 seconds and on originality

benchmarks.metric: Public numeric thresholds for watch time/sends/likes
benchmarks.context: Benchmark against the account's own trailing median. Third-party claims that sends weigh '3-5x' likes are unverified

entries.title: Instagram originality rules now cover Reels, photos and carousels: protect recommendation eligibility
entries.guidance: Since 30 April 2026, Instagram's originality protections apply to photos and carousels as well as Reels. Accounts that mainly post unoriginal material are removed from recommendation surfaces, though followers still see their posts. Adding a border, watermark, subtitles or a credit line does not make reposted content original. Original content means footage you shot, assets you designed, or third-party material you changed substantially by adding new information, context or a point of view, or by using Remix. An account becomes eligible again once most of its recent posts in a rolling 30-day window are original, and creators can check this, remove posts or appeal in Account Status. For a white-label AI system that serves many coaches, every tenant's content must be built from that coach's own footage, stories, client cases and frameworks, and the same asset must never be pushed to several accounts.
do: Generate scripts from each coach's own transcripts, call notes and frameworks, then have the coach film them
Use Remix or collabs for reaction content, and add real commentary or new data
Check Account Status weekly as part of the automated account-health check
Share other creators' work through Stories or reposts rather than re-uploading it to the grid
dont: Re-upload trending clips from other creators with only captions or credit added
Distribute identical AI-generated assets across multiple client accounts
Rely on watermark removal or speed changes to make content look original
steps: Tag every asset in the content library with its origin (self-filmed, designed, licensed, third-party)
Block publishing of third-party-origin assets unless they carry a material-edit flag (commentary, new data, Remix)
Each week, compute the share of the last 30 days' posts that are original and alert when it falls toward half
If an account is flagged, remove the unoriginal posts, appeal in Account Status, and post only original content for 30 days

benchmarks.metric: Share of US recommendations from original posts

benchmarks.value: Rolling 30 days, with 'most' recent posts original

entries.title: Use Instagram Trial Reels as a non-follower hook-testing lab
entries.guidance: Trial reels, rolled out to eligible creators from December 2024, are shown to non-followers first. They do not appear on the profile grid or in followers' feeds unless you share them. Views, likes, comments and shares appear about 24 hours after posting, together with a comparison against your earlier trials. You can share a winning trial manually or let Instagram auto-share it to followers if it gets strong views in its first 72 hours. This makes trial reels the cleanest available read on how cold audiences respond to a hook. Test one idea with two or three different openings and promote only the winner. The testing protocol below is our own synthesis, not Instagram guidance.
do: Keep the body of the video constant and vary only the first 3 seconds, the cover text or the opening line
Log the winning hook pattern (for example a pain question, a contrarian claim or a result-first opening) into a reusable hook library per coach
Turn on auto-share only for variants you would be happy for followers to see
dont: Assume trials are fully hidden: followers can still meet them through DM shares or audio and location pages
Treat one trial as conclusive: compare against the account's previous trials
Upload a near-identical copy of a reel that is already published, because Instagram makes already-posted reels less visible
steps: Script one idea with 2-3 distinct hooks
Post each variant as a trial (toggle Trial before sharing)
At about 24h, compare views, likes, shares and comments against the account's earlier trials
Share the winner with everyone (or let auto-share act within 72h) and archive the losers
Record the result in the hook library and reuse the pattern on the next idea

sources.title: Trial reels: Try content with non-followers first to see what performs best

entries.title: Short-form hook and retention spec: value in 3s, hook by 6s, 9:16, captions 5-10 words/sec
entries.guidance: TikTok's creative guidance (updated June 2025) says to state the content's value proposition within the first 3 seconds and land the hook within the first 6. It also recommends shooting vertical 9:16 at 720p or higher, using sound, adding captions or text at roughly 5-10 words per second, and preferring creator-style, less polished footage with one clear call to action. YouTube measures the 'intro' as the share of viewers still watching after 30 seconds. Its fix for weak intros is to make the title and thumbnail match the opening and to experiment with the first 30 seconds. For coaching content, open with the viewer's specific problem or desired outcome in their own words, show the payoff or proof early, teach one idea, and close with one CTA (keyword comment, follow, or watch the long-form video). TikTok's guidance was written for performance ads, so applying it to organic posts is an inference, but it agrees with the retention metrics every platform exposes.
do: Put the outcome or pain point on screen as text in the first frame
Burn in captions at 5-10 words/sec for sound-off viewers
Use a single CTA per video
Keep key text inside platform UI safe zones
dont: Open with greetings, logos or 'in this video I will...' preambles
Stack multiple CTAs (follow + comment + link) in one short
Use horizontal footage letterboxed into vertical
steps: Write hook options as: problem in the viewer's words, a counter-intuitive claim, or the result first
Make sure the first spoken line and on-screen text deliver the value proposition by second 3
Cut every pause and filler in the first 6 seconds
Add captions and check pacing against 5-10 words/sec
Review the retention curve: if the drop at 0-3s is steep, rework the hook; if it drops mid-video, cut that section

entries.title: YouTube Shorts: 3-minute limit, Content ID blocking over 1 minute, no clickable links, so route to long-form
entries.guidance: Square or vertical uploads of up to 3 minutes have counted as Shorts since 15 October 2024. Uploading at 16:9 keeps a video in long-form. Any Short longer than 1 minute that carries an active Content ID claim of any kind is blocked worldwide and cannot be played, recommended or monetized. Use original audio or the YouTube Audio Library for 1-3 minute Shorts; most Shorts Audio Library tracks are limited to 90 seconds, and some to 60 or 30. Links in Shorts descriptions and comments stopped being clickable on 31 August 2023. YouTube added clickable links near the Subscribe button on channel pages and announced a safer way to link a Short to long-form content. So the Short's job is to send viewers to a long-form video or to the channel page, not to an external URL.
do: Use Shorts as trailers for a specific long-form video and link that video to the Short with YouTube's related-video option
Keep 1-3 minute Shorts free of third-party music
Put the lead-magnet link in the channel-page links and in long-form video descriptions
dont: Paste URLs into Shorts descriptions expecting clicks
Use popular copyrighted tracks in Shorts longer than 60 seconds
Assume a 16:9 upload under 3 minutes will be treated as a Short
steps: For each long-form video, cut 2-4 vertical Shorts from its strongest moments
Attach the source long-form video as the related video on each Short
Close each Short with a verbal CTA to the full video
Check Studio for copyright claims before publishing any Short over 60 seconds

sources.title: YouTube's banning clickable links from Shorts descriptions and comments

entries.title: YouTube long-form as a pre-sales asset: valued watch time, chapters, retention fixes, clickable links
entries.guidance: YouTube's recommendation system aims at viewer satisfaction. Beyond clicks and watch time, it uses survey ratings as 'valued watchtime', and only 4- and 5-star ratings count. It also predicts shares and likes, and treats dislikes as a negative signal. For a coach, a long-form video works like a recorded pre-sales call: answer one high-intent buyer question in depth, show the method and evidence, handle the main objections, and invite one next step. Links stay clickable in long-form descriptions and comments, so put the lead-magnet or application link in the first lines of the description and in a pinned comment, and mention it out loud at natural breaks. Add manual chapters so prospects can jump to proof and objections. Then use the retention report's key moments to fix the opening, move top moments earlier and cut dips.
do: Title videos around a buyer's question or desired outcome, not the coach's jargon
Put chapters on case studies, the method and FAQs/objections
Place the CTA link in description line 1-2 and in a pinned comment
Turn top retention moments into new videos and Shorts
dont: Save all the value for the end: YouTube notes audiences shrink over a video's length
Use clickbait titles the opening doesn't pay off, which hurts the 30-second intro metric
Add chapters that break the rules (they won't render)
steps: Pick one buyer question per video from sales-call transcripts
Outline it as hook (matching the title/thumbnail promise), proof, method, objections, CTA
Add manual chapters starting at 00:00, with at least 3 timestamps, each chapter at least 10 seconds long
Publish with the lead-magnet link in the description and a pinned comment
After 1-2 days (once the video passes 100 views), review intro retention, top moments, spikes and dips, then iterate

benchmarks.value: Video >=60s and >=100 views; data in 1-2 days

sources.title: Measure key moments for audience retention
YouTube's banning clickable links from Shorts descriptions and comments

entries.title: YouTube native A/B testing: up to 3 title/thumbnail variants, judged on watch-time share
entries.guidance: YouTube Studio on desktop can test up to three titles, three thumbnails, or title-and-thumbnail pairs. The winner is chosen by watch-time share, not click-through rate, so a variant that wins clicks but loses viewers will not win. Results come back as Winner, Performed Same or Inconclusive. Tests run from a few days to about two weeks, depending on impressions and video age. Shorts, scheduled livestreams, Premieres (until they finish), made-for-kids, age-restricted and private videos cannot be tested. Changing the title or thumbnail during a test stops it. YouTube advises starting with older videos, making the variants meaningfully different, and uploading thumbnails at 1280x720 or larger.
do: Test clearly different angles (for example outcome vs. pain vs. curiosity), not small wording changes
Start with evergreen back-catalogue videos that still get impressions
Make sure every variant's promise matches the first 30 seconds of the video
dont: Edit the title or thumbnail mid-test
Use third-party CTR-only testers as the main decision tool for a sales asset
Upload thumbnails below 1280x720 (all variants are downscaled to 854x480)
steps: Pick a video with steady impressions
Create 2-3 distinct title/thumbnail concepts
Run the test in Studio's A/B testing panel for up to 2 weeks
Apply the winner, log the winning angle per niche, and reuse it on new uploads

entries.title: TikTok: originality for For You eligibility, and commercial disclosure even when promoting your own coaching
entries.guidance: Under TikTok's Community Guidelines (released 25 August 2026, effective 24 September 2026), unoriginal or reused material that adds nothing new is not eligible for the For You feed. Content that pushes people to inflate likes, follows or gifts is also ineligible. Ineligible videos can still show in search and on the profile, and analytics show whether a video was excluded. Creators must switch on the content disclosure setting when they promote their own business, product or service, as well as for branded or incentivised content. Undisclosed promotion can lose visibility or have the label applied by TikTok, and repeat failures can lead to posting restrictions or a ban. Financial scams, including 'get-rich-quick' schemes, and multi-level marketing are not allowed, so coaching offers about earning money need careful, substantiated framing.
do: Turn on content disclosure on any video that promotes the coach's own programme, call or paid product
Add genuine commentary or new information to any reused clip
Check each video's analytics for FYF-ineligibility flags
dont: Use 'follow for follow' or 'like to unlock' engagement mechanics
Frame offers as fast or guaranteed wealth
Repost other creators' content without new value
steps: Classify each post as educational, own-offer promotion or branded content before publishing
Have the publishing pipeline enable the disclosure toggle automatically for own-offer and branded posts
Run a claims check that blocks income promises and 'quick money' framing
Review FYF eligibility in analytics 24h after posting

entries.title: AI-assisted content: what must be labelled on YouTube and TikTok, and what is exempt
entries.guidance: YouTube requires creators to tick the 'AI use' setting for realistic altered or synthetic content. That covers making a real person seem to say or do something, altering real events or places, creating realistic scenes that never happened, and AI music that is the main focus of a video. Using AI for scripts, outlines, titles, thumbnails, infographics, idea generation, captions and audio repair does not need disclosure, and neither does cloning your own voice for a voiceover. YouTube may also auto-label content made with its tools, carrying C2PA metadata, or detected as AI. Disclosure alone does not reduce reach or monetization, but creators who consistently fail to disclose can be labelled, have content removed, or be suspended from the Partner Program. TikTok requires a label on AI-generated or heavily edited content showing realistic scenes or people. The FTC says AI avatars are not banned in themselves, but they must not deliver fake testimonials.
do: Build a per-asset 'realistic synthetic?' flag into the publishing pipeline and map it to each platform's disclosure toggle
Use AI freely for scripting, outlines, titles and thumbnails (exempt on YouTube)
Keep testimonials limited to real clients' own words and footage
dont: Generate realistic avatar 'clients' or fabricated results footage
Clone another person's likeness or voice
Strip C2PA metadata to avoid labels
steps: At generation time, record which assets contain realistic synthetic people, voices or scenes
Auto-set YouTube's AI-use disclosure and TikTok's AI label for flagged assets
Block any synthetic asset presented as a customer testimonial
Audit labels monthly against platform notifications in Studio

sources.title: Disclosing use of altered or synthetic content
Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule: Questions and Answers

entries.title: Instagram comment-keyword DMs: one private reply, 7-day limit, 24h window only after the user replies
entries.guidance: A DM triggered by a comment on Instagram is a Private Reply. Each commenter can receive only one, and it must be sent within 7 days of the comment; for Live, it can only be sent while the broadcast is running. A comment does not open a conversation. Follow-ups are allowed only after the person replies, and only within 24 hours of that reply. The standard window lasts 24 hours from the user's last action. Conversations that start from a Click-to-Direct ad can stay open for up to 7 days. The Human Agent tag gives a person, not a bot, a separate 7 days to answer. Messages to non-followers arrive in Requests rather than the Inbox. Using this requires an Instagram professional account and the comment and messaging permissions. An app serving accounts it does not own needs Advanced Access through App Review. Meta also says automated chats should disclose that they are automated, which is required by law in places such as California and Germany and recommended everywhere else.
do: Make the single private reply count: ask a question or offer a button so the user responds and opens the 24h window
Disclose automation in the first message ('automated assistant, a human can step in')
Hand off to a human (using the Human Agent tag) for sales conversations that go past 24h
Get Advanced Access before onboarding client accounts you don't own
dont: Send multiple automated messages to a commenter who has not replied
Use the Human Agent tag for automated sequences
Promise prospects ongoing DM drips on Instagram; move nurture to email
steps: Subscribe webhooks to comments (and live_comments)
On a matching keyword, send one private reply with a quick-reply or button prompt
On the user's response, deliver the resource and ask for email within 24h
Route high-intent replies to a human inbox (Conversation Routing; Handover Protocol is no longer supported for Instagram as of Oct 2025)
Log consent and the timestamp of every window-opening event

benchmarks.value: Up to 7 days from user's first message

entries.title: Instagram messaging throughput: 750 private replies/hour per account; plan queues for viral posts
entries.guidance: Meta's documented Instagram limits apply per professional account. Private Replies to post and reel comments are capped at 750 calls per hour, and replies to Live comments at 100 calls per second. The Send API allows 300 calls per second for text, links, reactions and stickers and 10 per second for audio or video, and the Conversations API allows 2 calls per second. Once an account has sent and received more than 72,000 messages, new messages stop appearing in the Inbox and sending is blocked until volume falls. The widely quoted '200 automated DMs per hour' cap does not appear in Meta's Instagram rate-limit documentation; treat it as a tool-side pacing convention. A post that draws 3,000 keyword comments in an hour therefore needs about 4 hours to clear, which is well inside the 7-day private-reply limit but slow enough to cost conversions. Meta's changelog also matters: three message tags (CONFIRMED_EVENT_UPDATE, ACCOUNT_UPDATE, POST_PURCHASE_UPDATE) returned errors from 27 April 2026.
do: Queue private replies with per-account pacing under 750/hour and prioritise the newest comments
Show 'sending your link now' expectations in the caption when a viral post is likely
Monitor the 72,000-message threshold on high-volume accounts
dont: Hard-code third-party '200/hour' or '5,000/hour' figures as Meta rules
Burst identical public comment replies, which risks spam filters
Rely on deprecated message tags for re-engagement
steps: Implement a per-account token bucket for private replies (750/hour) and the Send API
Alert when the queue delay goes past 30 minutes and suggest a story or broadcast fallback
Re-check Meta's rate-limit page and changelog each quarter

entries.title: Comment-keyword DM funnel design: earn the reply, capture email in 24h, nurture off-platform
entries.guidance: Instagram allows only one automated private reply per commenter, and nothing more until the person responds. The first DM should therefore earn a tap or reply rather than drop a bare link, because the response is what opens the 24-hour window for delivery and email capture. Once the window is open, deliver the promised resource, ask for an email address (with clear marketing consent), and ask one qualifying question. Longer nurture belongs in email, where you control the cadence. Tool vendors document that keyword triggers usually fire only on a user's first comment per post, so use a short, unique keyword per post and show it both on screen and in the caption. Public conversion numbers are mostly vendor case studies. One Manychat-published story reports 53,000 email leads and an 85% webinar-registration rate from comments over 12 months, but these figures are not independently verified, so each account should measure its own funnel stages.
do: Use one memorable keyword per post (e.g., a single word tied to the resource)
Make the first DM's question or button match the commenter's intent
Ask for email and one qualifier (role, revenue band, main goal) inside the window
Tag DM leads by source post for attribution
dont: Gate the resource behind a required follow or other engagement condition (check each platform's rules first)
Send the raw link as the only content of the one allowed private reply
Treat vendor case-study rates as targets
steps: Comment keyword triggers one private reply with a button or question
User taps or replies: deliver the resource link and request email with consent wording
Ask one qualifying question; high-fit answers get a booking or application link and a human alert
Sync the contact to the email platform's welcome sequence
Track the stages: comments, private replies sent, responses, emails captured, applications, calls booked

benchmarks.context: Manychat-published case study, unverified; not a neutral benchmark

entries.title: Email deliverability 2025-26: SPF+DKIM+DMARC, spam rate <0.1%, one-click unsubscribe honoured in 48h
entries.guidance: Gmail and Yahoo require every sender to authenticate with SPF or DKIM, keep valid forward and reverse DNS, use TLS (Gmail) and send RFC-compliant messages. Bulk senders must have SPF and DKIM, publish DMARC (p=none is acceptable), and align the From domain with SPF or DKIM. Gmail defines a bulk sender as one that sends close to 5,000 or more messages a day to personal Gmail accounts, and the status is permanent once reached. Keep the user-reported spam rate below 0.1% and never let it reach 0.3%. Above 0.3%, Gmail withholds mitigation until the rate stays under it for 7 consecutive days, and Gmail began ramping up enforcement in November 2025, including temporary and permanent rejections. Marketing mail needs one-click unsubscribe (List-Unsubscribe plus List-Unsubscribe-Post, per RFC 8058) and a visible unsubscribe link, with requests honoured within 48 hours or 2 days. Microsoft rejects mail from senders of 5,000+ messages to its consumer domains that fails its authentication requirements, with error 550 5.7.515.
do: Use a dedicated sending subdomain per coach/tenant with its own SPF, DKIM and DMARC
Monitor Google Postmaster Tools spam rate daily and pause campaigns as it approaches 0.1%
Process unsubscribes in real time, well inside 48h
Warm new domains gradually (Gmail applies an accelerated timetable to new domains)
dont: Send from free-mail From addresses (e.g., @gmail.com) through an ESP
Import purchased or scraped lists
Hide the unsubscribe link or require a login to unsubscribe
steps: Publish SPF, DKIM (2048-bit recommended) and DMARC p=none with a rua reporting address, then check alignment
Enable RFC 8058 one-click headers in the ESP
Register the domain in Google Postmaster Tools and monitor Microsoft authentication results
Set an automatic brake: if spam rate >0.08%, send only to engaged segments until it recovers
Sunset subscribers who haven't clicked in 90-180 days (practitioner convention)

entries.title: Email consent law for lead magnets: CAN-SPAM basics, UK specific-consent rule, opt-outs
entries.guidance: US CAN-SPAM rules: no misleading headers or subject lines, mark the message as an advertisement, include a valid physical postal address, and give a clear opt-out. Opt-outs must be honoured within 10 business days, the mechanism must keep working for at least 30 days after sending, and it cannot charge a fee or ask for more than an email address. Each violating email can draw penalties of up to $53,088 (the January 2024 figure, adjusted for inflation each year). The UK rule is stricter: marketing email to individuals needs specific consent to hear from you. The 'soft opt-in' covers only people who bought, or discussed buying, a similar product and were offered an opt-out. Someone who only downloaded a freebie is not covered, so lead-magnet forms need clear consent wording. The ICO says its guidance is under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act. This is a summary, not legal advice.
do: Add explicit consent wording on every lead-magnet form ('you'll also get emails from X; unsubscribe anytime')
Store consent source, timestamp, IP and form version per contact
Include a postal address and a working unsubscribe link in every marketing email
Keep a suppression list that is checked before every send and import
dont: Assume a freebie download gives UK/EU marketing consent without disclosure
Ask subscribers to submit friends' emails
Sell or share opted-out addresses
steps: Detect the subscriber's region at signup and apply the stricter consent template where needed
Log a consent record for each contact
Process unsubscribes immediately (this meets the 48h mailbox-provider rule and the 10-business-day legal rule)
Review legal templates whenever ICO, FTC or CRTC guidance changes

benchmarks.context: FTC figure as of Jan 2024; inflation-adjusted annually

sources.title: CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business

entries.title: Email and newsletter benchmarks for coaching: judge on clicks, not opens
entries.guidance: MailerLite's 2025 medians, from 3.6 million campaigns sent December 2024 to November 2025, are a 43.46% open rate, 2.09% click rate, 6.81% click-to-open rate and 0.22% unsubscribe rate. Coaching senders had above-average opens (48.07%) but below-average clicks (1.42%), a lower CTOR (4.9%) and higher unsubscribes (0.3%). That pattern suggests coaching emails get opened but often lack a compelling click. beehiiv's report on 2025 data puts platform opens above 41% and gives a median of 66 days to first revenue for newsletters launched in 2025. Mailbox privacy features inflate open rates, so treat click rate, CTOR and replies as the real health metrics. These are vendor platform medians, not neutral industry data.
do: Set KPIs on click rate and CTOR per email and per sequence
Give each email one primary link and one job
Use reply-prompt emails ('reply with your #1 bottleneck') to build engagement signals and gather lead intelligence
dont: Report open rate as the success metric to clients
Compare a coach's list against e-commerce averages
steps: Compute 30-day rolling click rate, CTOR and unsubscribe rate per tenant
Flag accounts with clicks below about 1.4% or unsubscribes above about 0.3% (coaching medians) for a copy and offer review
Test the subject line and the first-screen CTA separately

benchmarks.metric: Online courses open / click / CTOR / unsub
Median days to first revenue (new newsletters)

entries.title: Automated nurture sequences outperform broadcasts by a wide margin: build the welcome flow first
entries.guidance: Omnisend's 2025 dataset (more than 20 billion campaign emails and 470 million automated sends) shows automated emails with a 4.66% click rate against 0.74% for campaigns. Automations converted at 1.49% against 0.08%, and earned about $3.41 per email against $0.155. Welcome series did best among automations, at a 2.11% conversion rate and 11.19% CTOR. The data is e-commerce, so for coaching read 'conversion' as booked calls or applications, but the gap between triggered and broadcast email is large enough to set priorities. MailerLite also reports much higher open rates for automations. Build the trigger-based welcome and lead-magnet sequences before investing in a weekly newsletter. The sequence below is a practitioner starting point, not a benchmarked standard.
do: Trigger the sequence on the specific lead magnet or keyword so the first emails continue that exact topic
Include one case story with documented, typical results and one objection-handling email
Put the booking or application CTA in every email after the first, framed as an option
dont: Send new leads straight into a generic weekly newsletter
Use countdown urgency that isn't real (see the FTC entries)
Let sequences run on after a lead books a call: branch them on booking status
steps: Email 0 (immediately): deliver the resource with one quick-win action
Day 1: the core belief shift or framework behind the resource
Day 2-3: a documented client case story (with typicality context)
Day 4-5: objections and FAQs, plus an invitation to apply or book
Day 6-7: a direct 'is this for you / not for you' email with the CTA
Then move to the newsletter, with re-entry triggers on high-intent clicks

entries.title: Lead-magnet opt-in pages: median about 6.6%; education and online-course pages convert higher; keep copy short and plain
entries.guidance: Unbounce's benchmark covers more than 41,000 landing pages, 464 million visitors and 57 million conversions between July 2023 and July 2024. It found a median conversion rate of 6.6% across industries and 8.4% for education. Online-course pages had a median of 18.3% and general course pages 13%. In education, email-sourced traffic converted best (14.1%), ahead of paid search (7.3%) and paid social (5.1%). Mobile made up about 85% of education traffic but converted below desktop (10.2% vs 12%). Copy at a 12th-grade reading level or simpler converted 54% to more than 2x better than college-level copy, and education pages needed the fewest words of any industry, about 363 words to reach the median. For coaches, this points to a single specific promise, a short mobile-first page, and plain language.
do: Promise one specific, quick result (a checklist, script, template or short training)
Write at or below a 12th-grade reading level and keep pages around or under 300-400 words
Design for mobile first, then check desktop
Send email and DM traffic to the page (the highest-converting sources)
dont: Ask for more fields than you will use in the first week
Offer broad 'ultimate guides' with no concrete outcome
Use jargon-heavy copy
steps: Choose a lead magnet that solves a sub-problem of the paid offer
Write a headline with outcome and timeframe, 3 bullets, a form (email plus optional one qualifier) and a consent line
Score readability and word count before publishing
Track opt-in rate by traffic source and A/B test the headline first

benchmarks.metric: Word count to hit education median

entries.title: Content-to-call pipeline: instrument every hop and route all platforms into an owned list
entries.guidance: The most reliable organic path for a coach is: content, then a keyword DM or link, then a lead magnet and email capture, then an automated nurture, then an application or booking, then the call. Each hop has a measurable rate and a known failure mode. There are no neutral, public 2025-26 benchmarks for coaching show-up or close rates, so the system should build each tenant's own baselines rather than quote industry numbers. The verified reference points are opt-in pages (about 6.6% median, higher for email traffic), automated email (welcome series converting at about 2.11% in e-commerce data) and platform rules that cap what DMs can do. Short-form content mostly creates reach, while YouTube long-form and email carry most of the trust-building before a call, so send call CTAs mainly from long-form, nurture emails and qualified DM conversations.
do: Use UTM parameters or keyword-to-source mapping on every CTA
Qualify before the calendar: an application or at least one qualifier question
Send pre-call assets (a long-form video and a case study) after booking
Report weekly by stage: reach, leads, applications, booked, showed, closed
dont: Push cold short-form viewers straight to a sales call link
Quote vendor or 'guru' close rates as expectations to clients
Optimise booked calls without tracking show rate and fit
steps: Map each content piece to one CTA destination
Capture source on every lead (post ID, keyword, video ID)
Run the nurture sequence with the booking CTA, branched on clicks
Calculate stage conversion each week and fix the weakest stage first
Feed call-outcome reasons (no-fit, price, timing) back into content topics

entries.title: FTC enforcement on business-coaching marketing: no unsubstantiated income, 'no experience', urgency or AI claims
entries.guidance: The FTC keeps suing money-making and business-coaching sellers. In January 2026 the Growth Cave defendants, whose alleged consumer harm was about $50 million, agreed to orders banning them from selling business opportunities and from misleading claims about earnings, testimonials and artificial intelligence. In March 2026, Air AI and its owners settled allegations of unsupported earnings claims and refund or buy-back guarantees that were not honoured. That settlement carries an $18 million judgment (largely suspended), a ban on selling business opportunities, and a bar on earnings claims without substantiation. The FTC's 2021 Notice of Penalty Offenses, sent to more than 1,100 companies including business coaches, puts marketers on notice that civil penalties can follow from false earnings claims, claims that represented results are typical, false 'no experience needed' claims, false urgency, and misleading testimonials. For an AI that writes content, DMs and sales scripts for coaches, these are hard guardrails rather than style preferences.
do: Run every generated asset through a claims filter for income figures, guarantees, 'anyone can', 'no experience' and time-bound wealth promises
Pair any result example with substantiation and typicality context, kept on file
State refund terms exactly as the contract says and honour them
Describe AI capabilities only as demonstrated
dont: Use phrases like 'six figures in 90 days' or 'replace your income'
Present outlier student results as typical
Invent deadlines or scarcity
Let setters, closers or affiliates use scripts with stronger claims than the approved copy (the bans also cover assisting others)
steps: Maintain a banned-claims lexicon plus an LLM classifier on all outbound copy
Require a substantiation record ID for any numeric result claim
Log approvals of compliance-sensitive copy per tenant
Audit DM and call-script outputs monthly

entries.title: Testimonials and social proof: FTC rule bans fake reviews, sentiment-conditioned incentives and fake follower/view counts
entries.guidance: The FTC's Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule took effect on 21 October 2024. It bans writing, buying or selling fake or false reviews and testimonials. Incentives cannot be tied to a positive sentiment, even if the incentive is disclosed. Testimonials from insiders such as staff, executives or their relatives need a clear disclosure of the relationship. Reviews cannot be suppressed through threats or false accusations. Buying or knowingly spreading fake followers, views or other indicators of influence is also banned. AI avatars are not banned outright, but an avatar that delivers a fake testimonial or uses someone's likeness without permission can break the rule. Courts can impose civil penalties for knowing violations. For a coaching system that automates case studies and social proof, every testimonial must trace back to a real, consenting client.
do: Collect testimonials through a consent form that records the client's identity, date and permission
Ask all clients for reviews, not only happy ones
Disclose staff or affiliate relationships in any testimonial they give
dont: Generate or 'polish' testimonials beyond light editing that keeps the meaning
Offer bonuses for 5-star reviews only
Buy followers, views or engagement pods for any client account
steps: Store testimonial source media and the consent record
Tag testimonials with typicality context when they include results
Block publication of any testimonial without a linked consent record
